# Link

Figma: [02c. Link](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-891) · Family: 02 Actions · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-19

A Link is an inline navigation control - text that takes the user to another location. Unlike Button, Link is NOT for actions in the current context (submit, save, delete) - it is for moving the user somewhere else (a route, a URL, a document). The Flutter and HTML semantics differ: Link should be implemented with InkWell + GestureDetector OR RichText with TapGestureRecognizer in Flutter, and as <a href> in web prototypes. Screen readers announce links and buttons differently - getting this distinction right matters for accessibility.

### Link

Inline underlined text that navigates to another route, URL or document. It moves the user somewhere else and never changes state in the current context.

Level: organism

Use when:
- Opening terms, the CMA disclosure, the Sharia board page or a glossary entry from body copy: Variant=info or default
- Downloading an offering file or statement PDF: leading document icon
- External destinations such as safqah.co: trailing arrow-up-right icon
- Low-priority paths like «لاحقاً» or Skip this step: Variant=muted

Don't use when:
- The click submits, saves, confirms or deletes in place: use Button (Variant=text for an inline-looking action)
- Async work with a loading state is needed: use Button
- A row in a settings list that opens a detail screen: use ListItem with a chevron

Accessibility: Keep Underline on (the default green fails AA contrast in light mode without it) and announce it as a link, with a hint when it opens outside the app.

> Not published to the Figma library. Use it by name everywhere; in another Figma file take its published route or copy it from the Syntropy file (syntropy-components, unpublished.md).

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

A Link is an inline navigation control - it takes the user from where they are to somewhere else. That "somewhere else" can be a route in your app (/portfolio/123), an external URL (https://safqah.co/terms), a deep link to a different screen, or a document download. The visual treatment is text-based: a colored, underlined word or phrase that reads as a link, not as a button.

The Link vs Button distinction is semantic, not visual. A Button triggers an action in the current context (submit form, delete row, confirm dialog). A Link navigates. If clicking it changes the URL or pushes a new route, it is a Link. If clicking it submits data or modifies state without navigating, it is a Button. Screen readers announce these differently, and right-click behavior differs on the web - getting the distinction right matters.

### Live preview - one of each variant

### Anatomy

A Link is a HORIZONTAL auto-layout frame containing an optional leading icon, a label text node, and an optional trailing icon. The whole component has no chrome - no fill, no border, no padding (except in focused state where a 4px ring breathing room is added). The label carries the text color of the variant and an underline by default.

**1. Leading icon (optional)**
Toggled via Has icon leading. Common patterns: document icon for "Download the report", external-link arrow before a domain name in a footer.

**2. Label**
The link text. Bound to the Label property and overridable per instance. Underlined by default (governed by the Underline boolean property - toggle off when the link sits inline with body text and the underline would create visual noise).

**3. Trailing icon (optional)**
Toggled via Has icon trailing. Most common pattern: arrow-up-right (↗) for external links, chevron-right for "in-app" navigation, download icon for file links.

### Variants

Four variants cover the navigation intents Safqah needs. Pick by the meaning of the destination, not by the look. A default Link in green communicates "trusted internal navigation"; an inverse Link in white communicates "use me on a dark background." Choose based on context.

| Default Green underlined text, color = text/brand/primary. Standard navigation link tone - communicates "this is a Safqah-managed destination, click with confidence." | When to use Internal route navigation, in-app navigation, trusted external resources (Saudi DGA, Sharia council, official partners). Most links in the app should be this. |
| --- | --- |

| Info Blue underlined text, color = text/info. Visually neutral and informational - signals the destination contains supplementary, non-actionable content. | When to use Legal pages, "Learn more" links, glossary entries, policy documents, terms of service, footnote citations. Anywhere the link is for reading, not for doing. |
| --- | --- |

| Danger Red underlined text, color = text/error. The destructive equivalent of a destructive Button - but for navigations that lead to irreversible actions. | When to use Inline destructive options in settings paragraphs ("Click here to permanently delete your account"). Always pair with a confirmation step on the destination page. |
| --- | --- |

| Inverse White underlined text, color = text/on-brand. Designed for use on dark or high-saturation backgrounds where the default green would not have enough contrast. | When to use Footer navigation on a dark background, links inside a dark hero banner, links inside the inverse-mode Toast or Alert components. |
| --- | --- |

| Primary text Dark underlined text, color = text/default. The link reads as body copy - only the underline signals it's clickable. The quietest tone available for inline navigation while staying clearly readable. Passes WCAG AAA at 17.5:1. | When to use Inline links inside dense paragraphs where the green default is too loud. Table-of-contents anchors. Footnote citations. Author bylines. Anywhere the link should integrate into prose rather than stand apart from it. |
| --- | --- |

| Muted text Gray underlined text, color = text/muted. The lowest-emphasis link variant - readable but visually de-emphasized. Passes WCAG AA at 6.7:1 in light mode and AAA in dark mode. | When to use De-prioritized navigation: "Skip this step", "Maybe later", "Dismiss", footer legal references, supplementary "related articles" links. Anywhere the link must exist but should never compete with the primary path. |
| --- | --- |

### Sizes

Three sizes match the Button text scale exactly. Pick by matching the surrounding text. A link inside a paragraph should match the paragraph's body-text size; a link in a dense list footer should match the smaller list typography.

Large (lg)

| Font size | 16px |
| --- | --- |
| Icon size | 20px |
| Font weight | Medium |
| Underline | On by default |
Medium (md) · default

| Font size | 14px |
| --- | --- |
| Icon size | 18px |
| Font weight | Medium |
| Underline | On by default |
Small (sm)

| Font size | 13px |
| --- | --- |
| Icon size | 16px |
| Font weight | Medium |
| Underline | On by default |

### States

Five states: default, hover, pressed, focused, disabled. Note there is no "loading" state - links don't typically trigger async actions in the current context; if you need that pattern, use a Button instead. There is also no "visited" state - Flutter doesn't track visited links natively; if you need this for a web context, the engineer must track it manually.

Default

Resting state. Underlined and in the variant text color.

Hover

Cursor is over the link (web/desktop only). Same underline; the surrounding cursor changes to pointer.

Pressed

User is actively clicking/tapping. Brief visual press feedback.

Focused

2px outline ring with 4px padding around the link. Outline binds to border/focus → text/default for max contrast.

Disabled

Cannot be activated. Color shifts to text/disabled, underline removed (avoids the dead-link look).

### Direction handling - RTL

Link does NOT ship with a Direction variant axis. Inline text inherits its parent's text direction automatically - when wrapped in Directionality(textDirection: TextDirection.rtl), the label re-flows right-to-left and the leading/trailing icons swap their visual position via the HORIZONTAL auto-layout.

For directional icons (chevron-right used for "in-app navigation arrow"), pick the correct icon at the call site based on Directionality.of(context) - same pattern as IconButton. The Link container itself is direction-agnostic.

> **Info:** For Arabic copy, replace the Label text with Arabic (e.g. "عرض المزيد" instead of "View more"). The underline renders correctly in RTL - it sits under the Arabic text just as it would under Latin.

> **Warning:** When inserting a Link inline with a body paragraph, ensure the parent Text widget has the correct textDirection. A Link in a paragraph with mixed Arabic and English (e.g. "Visit safqah.co for details") needs careful handling of bidirectional text - the Link itself does not solve this; the surrounding text widget must.

### Icons

Icons are optional in Links and used sparingly. The two common patterns:

Trailing arrow-up-right (↗)

Signals an external destination - clicking opens a new tab or leaves the app. Use arrow-up-right from the Syntropy Icons library trailing the label. Pair with target="_blank" / Flutter url_launcher in code.

Leading document or download icon

Signals the link is to a downloadable file or a PDF document. Use document/download icon leading the label so the user sees the icon before reading the text.

> **Tip:** Don't add icons to most navigation links. A plain colored, underlined "View deal" reads as navigation by convention alone - adding a chevron-right adds visual noise without adding meaning. Reserve icons for the two patterns above where they communicate destination type.

### Code examples

How engineering consumes Link in production code.

### Flutter / Dart

```dart
// Internal route navigation
SafqahLink(
  label: 'View deal details',
  variant: SafqahLinkVariant.default,
  size: SafqahLinkSize.md,
  href: '/deals/${dealId}',
  onTap: () => Navigator.pushNamed(context, '/deals/$dealId'),
)

// External link (opens in browser)
SafqahLink(
  label: 'safqah.co',
  variant: SafqahLinkVariant.default,
  hasIconTrailing: true,
  iconTrailing: SafqahIcons.arrowUpRight,
  href: 'https://safqah.co',
  onTap: () => launchUrl(Uri.parse('https://safqah.co')),
)

// Destructive link inline in settings
SafqahLink(
  label: 'Permanently delete your account',
  variant: SafqahLinkVariant.danger,
  href: '/settings/delete-account',
  onTap: () => _showConfirmAndDelete(),
)
```

### React / TypeScript (web prototype)

```typescript
// Internal route - wrap with react-router Link
<RouterLink to="/portfolio">
  <Link variant="default" size="md">View portfolio</Link>
</RouterLink>

// External link
<Link
  href="https://safqah.co"
  target="_blank"
  rel="noopener noreferrer"
  variant="default"
  hasIconTrailing
  iconTrailing={<ArrowUpRightIcon />}
>
  safqah.co
</Link>
```

### Build / CLI

```bash
# Generate Link widget from design tokens
flutter pub run safqah_codegen:tokens --component=Link

# Static analysis: confirm Links use href, not bare onTap
flutter analyze --rules=require_link_href
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Concrete Link scenarios from real Safqah surfaces. The recurring theme: Link is for navigation; Button is for action. When in doubt, ask whether the click changes the URL/route or modifies state - if it modifies state, you want Button instead.

- **Do** · Scenario · Inline in body paragraph: Default green link inline with paragraph text. Underline makes it clearly clickable even when colors blend with surrounding body text.
- **Don't** · Scenario · Inline in body paragraph: Using a primary Button for an inline link breaks the prose flow. The chrome screams "main action" when this is really a navigation to a legal page. Use Link variant default.
- **Do** · Scenario · Delete account in settings: Danger link signals the destination is destructive. The red color slows the user down. Confirmation should live on the destination page.
- **Don't** · Scenario · Delete account in settings: Default green link for a destructive navigation reads as "safe to click." Users may proceed accidentally. Use the danger variant.
- **Do** · Scenario · External link to safqah.co: Default link with trailing arrow-up-right icon signals "external, opens in browser." Pair with target="_blank" in code so a new tab opens.
- **Don't** · Scenario · External link to safqah.co: Same link without the external-link indicator. Users click expecting in-app navigation and instead get yanked to the browser. Always signal external destinations.
- **Do** · Scenario · Forgot password: Default-style link sized down to sm. Sits inline next to the login form, reads as a secondary path without competing with the primary Submit button.
- **Don't** · Scenario · Forgot password: Oversized link at lg next to login form looks as important as the Sign in CTA. The user pauses to figure out priority. Use sm to match secondary path emphasis.
- **Do** · Scenario · Footer navigation on dark background: Inverse variant on dark footer chrome. White underlined text has AAA contrast on bg/inverse. Both links sized at sm to read as footer-tier.
- **Don't** · Scenario · Footer navigation on dark background: Default green links on a dark footer background fail contrast - they become unreadable or look like decoration. Use the inverse variant on dark surfaces.
- **Do** · Scenario · "Learn more" expander in onboarding: Info variant (blue) signals educational content. The blue distinguishes "supplementary reading" from "navigate to take action," and matches the calm tone of onboarding.
- **Don't** · Scenario · "Learn more" expander in onboarding: Danger variant on educational content reads as a warning. Users expect a destructive consequence and hesitate. Use info variant for "learn more" patterns.

### Notes from the maintainer

Six things to internalize before reaching for Link.

> **Info:** The Link-vs-Button decision: does the click change the URL/route or modify state? If it changes location, Link. If it changes state, Button. Edge case: "Logout" can read either way - convention says Button, since logout modifies session state and doesn't navigate to a meaningful "logout page."

> **Warning:** Default variant fails WCAG AA in light mode at 2.79:1. Mitigations: use Info or Danger variants where appropriate; place links on bg/elevated for slightly better contrast; bold the link text in paragraphs to reach AA Large threshold. The underline is the secondary affordance signal - never turn it off on the default variant in light mode.

> **Tip:** For external links: always use trailing arrow-up-right (↗) icon, always open in a new tab (target="_blank" / launchUrl), always set Semantics(link: true, hint: "opens in browser"). Users should know what kind of destination they're heading to.

> **Info:** RTL works automatically via parent text direction - no Direction variant axis needed. The HORIZONTAL auto-layout flips icon positions, and the underline renders correctly under Arabic. For directional icons inside a link, pick the right one at the call site based on Directionality.of(context).

> **Warning:** Anti-patterns: (1) using a Button when a Link is right (and vice versa) - breaks screen reader semantics. (2) using Default variant on dark backgrounds - fails contrast catastrophically. (3) removing the underline - kills the accessibility-safe affordance signal. (4) inline Links at sm size in mobile touch contexts - fails touch target rules. (5) external links without the ↗ icon - disorients users when a new tab opens.

> **Tip:** External resources to internalize: NN/g's Links vs Buttons article (linked above), WCAG 2.4.4 on link purpose. Internal: Syntropy Icons library for icons, Safqah Brand Guidelines for link copy tone.
